unit.why: A brief narrative: R. A. of Kozienice relates in his master's name that the master passed a water mill and saw a dead man who had been close to a tzaddik standing under the turning wheel.
unit.boundary_note: Story ends abruptly with no explanation; it may be truncated. The next division (נז) is a separate story.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי אומרים כי אדמו״ר הה״ק המפורסם
stories.summary_en: The tzaddik of Kozienice told in his master's name that, passing a water mill, the master saw under the turning wheel, with water pouring on him, the soul of a man who in his lifetime had been close to a certain tzaddik.

tags.why: Framed as a tale told by the Kozienice tzaddik in his master's name

quotes: וראה איש א׳ עומד תחת הגלגל
tags.why: The master sees a dead man's soul that others cannot see

quotes: עומד תחת הגלגל כשהיה מגלגל ושופך מים
tags.why: Standing under the turning wheel implies posthumous suffering or punishment
The soul is bound to a material place after death, a possible gilgul-type punishment
The man is already dead; his death is implied, not depicted
Closeness to a tzaddik is the point, and it did not spare him
